proof_scope: In progress. Actual low/high-frequency L2 components are constructed, with exact Fourier representative formulas, norm contraction, and an exact low-component energy identity. For a normalized unit-supported real L2 input with zero K-cell means, 2048*pi^2*R^3<=K^2 makes the low component norm <=1/16. If original average correlation is >=1/2, the complementary component g has norm <=1, no Fourier mass on [-R,R], distance <=1/16 from the original complexified input, and real-inner-product correlation >=95/256>1/4. This is an explicit sharp-cutoff high-frequency reduction; smooth Littlewood-Paley band isolation and the spectral-gap contradiction remain.
